The lighting is dim and moody, dominated by cool tones like gray, slate blue, and white, emphasizing the eerie and desolate atmosphere.

Gradually, the fog begins to disperse in layers, uncovering the silhouette of Sun Wukong (S1). He emerges first with his golden cudgel held firmly, cautiously scouting the road ahead. His petite yet agile figure contrasts sharply against the vast, oppressive scenery. Head and shoulders of Tang Sanzang appear next, slumped in the saddle of the white horse. His weary posture implies exhaustion but remains distinctly identifiable.

The cold environment begins to gradually unfold more details as the fog lifts further. Zhu Bajie (S2), an extremely broad-bodied figure, appears next, carrying his nine-toothed rake and holding the reins of the white horse. Following him closely is Sha Wujing (S3), towering over the rest, carrying a heavy black wooden carrying pole and maintaining his posture with clear exertion. The pure white dragon horse, prominently positioned in the center, brings Tang Sanzang to the highest visual point relative to others. As the group progresses slowly, their heavily defined silhouettes begin blending into the bleak environment, becoming clearly discernible against an increasingly visible rocky pathway. The arrangement strictly adheres to their height and proportions: Tang Sanzang atop the white dragon horse remains the tallest, Sha Wujing follows, Zhu Bajie's broad presence takes precedence in width, and Sun Wukong’s stature is the most agile and lean.
